A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the surface geometry, the fluid properties (viscosity, surface tension, density and thermal conductivity), the Reynolds number and the surface tension gradients are the main parameters influencing the flow patterns, the Marangoni effects, and the heat and mass transfer processes.
the wire screen is a promising surface for absorption processes and 2-ethyl-hexanol is a promising additive for absorption processes.
2-ethyl-hexanol is an efficient additive in LiBr-water solution for heat and mass transfer augmentation, and that the wire screen is not a good surface for heat and mass augmentation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the heat and mass transfer characteristics of LiBr–water falling films can be significantly improved by the use of a wire screen surface and 2-ethyl-hexanol additive.
the heat transfer coefficients of the falling films of pure water and 50 wt.% LiBr-water solution can be enhanced by 2-3 times by adding 2-ethyl-hexanol.
the use of a surfactants can be an alternative to the use of a wire screen in order to improve the absorption of heat and water vapor from air.
